precepts.text: For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little; this is how we read the Bible.
precepts.point: On how to properly read the Bible: precept upon precept, line upon line, here a little and there a little. You can read from the back to get the history, and then precept upon precept, where reading one part explains another. Different parts of the Bible explain different things.

note.label: Psalm 150: Let Every Thing That Hath Breath Praise the Most High

precepts.why:
“Let every thing that hath breath praise the Lord.” This is the same thing read in Psalm 148: all the living of the earth praise the Most High. When Christ returns and the kingdom is delivered unto the Israelites, then every living thing on this earth is going to praise the Most High, even the sun, the moon, and the stars, which will do the same thing.

That is how the Bible is properly read: “For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little”. You can read from the back to get the history, and then precept upon precept, where reading one part explains another. Different parts of the Bible explain different things, and Psalm 148 explains Psalm 150.

points: Praise the Most High in His sanctuary; praise Him in the firmament of His power. Praise Him for His mighty acts; praise Him according to His excellent greatness.

note.label: Psalm 150: Let Every Thing That Hath Breath Praise the Most High

points: Praise Him with the sound of the trumpet, with the psaltery and harp, with the timbrel and dance, with stringed instruments and organs, upon the loud cymbals and the high sounding cymbals.
